newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: UAE forms shareholding firm for satellite project.
newsitem.headline: UAE forms shareholding firm for satellite project.

text.p: A United Arab Emirates-based shareholding company was formed on Monday to operate and own a major new satellite project for mobile communications, an official said.
The satellite project, called Al-Thurayya, is due to be operational by the turn of the century, he added.

"Today we have concluded the investment agreements and the legal documents in order to apply for the incorporation of the Al-Thurayya Satellite Telecommunications Company," project manager Hatim Lutfi told reporters.
The company has a starting capital of $25 million, he added.

Etisalat, the UAE's telecommunications heavyweight in which the government owns 60 percent, has projected that the company's capital would be raised to $500 million within six months, but Lutfi said he did not expect it to climb that high. He gave no specific figures.

He said Etisalat holds a 26 percent stake in the Al-Thurayya Satellite Telecommunications Company and the Arab Satellite Communications Organisation (Arabsat) owns 10 percent. Arabsat, which operates satellite telecommunications for Arab countries, is jointly owned by 21 Arab states.
Other shareholders include Bahrain Telecommunications Co (10 percent) and Germany's Detecom (0.5 percent), he said.
Officials have said the total cost of the satellite project would be around $800 million.
The Al-Thurayya satellite will provide services to UAE users of two-way mobile telephones compatible with the Global System for Mobile Communications (GSM).
It will make services available to remote sea and rural areas and will cover most Arab states, parts of the Indian subcontinent, Central Asia, North Africa and parts of Europe.
Lutfi said four telecommunications giants were competing to build the satellite system -- France's Alcatel and Aerospatiale, the United States' Hughes Electronics Corp and Lockheed Martin Corp.
He said he expected a deal to be signed by mid-1997.
